document_check.note: Overton M, Sjogren B, Elmstahl S, Rosso A. Mild Cognitive Impairment, Reversion Rates, and Associated Factors: Comparison of Two Diagnostic Approaches. J Alzheimers Dis 2023;91:585-601 (Good Aging in Skane cohort, Sweden). The age IRR 1.02 (1.01; 1.03), the reversion rates and the same-participant sensitivity analysis are all present.

cited_result: Principal result: the association of age at first MCI classification with incident reversion under the Petersen criteria in a multivariable Poisson model, IRR 1.02 (95% CI 1.01 to 1.03), n = 744. Also cited: the operational MCI definition, the similar primary reversion rates (43.4% Petersen vs 48.3% NP) and the divergence in the same-participant sensitivity analysis (32.9% vs 46.4%, n = 334).
tool_reason: The principal cited result is the association of one factor (age) with a later outcome (reversion) inside an adjusted model, not the performance of a prediction model, so QUIPS fits.

domains.rationale: The cohort is a random sample from the population register, but 30 to 40% of those invited did not take part. The reversion analysis is also restricted to MCI cases who were eligible at a follow-up visit.

signalling.question: Description of the source population and method of sampling?
signalling.quote: Participants from five municipalities in southern Sweden are randomly selected from the Swedish population register, and a new baseline cohort is added every sixth year.

signalling.question: Adequate participation by eligible persons?
signalling.quote: Participation rates varies between 60–70%.

signalling.question: Baseline study sample (period, place, inclusion) described?
signalling.quote: Between 2001 and 2020, 5,804 participants were examined, and during this period 1,785 and 987 were classified as MCI according the Petersen and Neuropsychological criteria, respectively.

signalling.question: Key characteristics of the sample described?
signalling.quote: Mean age for the first MCI diagnosis was 68 years of age, and women were slightly overrepresented regardless of the applied criteria (Table 1).

domains.rationale: Only 744 of 1,785 Petersen MCI cases entered the analysis. Those excluded (lost to follow-up, ADL decline, progression to dementia) were older, and the authors themselves attribute the age association to healthier older adults returning selectively. So attrition is linked to both the factor and the outcome.

signalling.question: Proportion of baseline sample with outcome data adequate?
signalling.quote: Of those participants a further 1,258/663 had at least one follow-up visit with 744/375 eligible to fulfil the applied MCI criteria at a subsequent follow-up visit

signalling.question: Reasons for loss to follow-up or exclusion provided?
signalling.quote: these 1,785/987 participants were followed until they either: 1) reverted, 2) no longer met MCI criteria (ADL worsened, no longer reported a cognitive complaint), 3) progressed to dementia, 4) were lost to follow-up, whichever event occurred first

signalling.question: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out?
signalling.quote: About 30% were lost to follow-up. Frail participants are less likely to attend follow-up visits, which could produce higher reversion rates since the healthiest returned to follow-up visits. To mitigate this effect, home visits were offered.

signalling.question: No important differences between completers and non-completers on the prognostic factor or outcome?
signalling.quote: Participants lost to follow-up, and ineligible for the application of the chosen MCI criteria (missing data or ADL-dependent), were somewhat older but otherwise had similar characteristics as those remaining in the study.

signalling.question: Does the source link the cited association to selective follow-up?
signalling.quote: older age was associated with reversion. This probably reflects a study design feature where healthy individuals are more prone to attend follow-up examinations and therefore cognitively preserved older adults are overrepresented in our sample.

domains.rationale: Age is clearly defined, measured at the first MCI classification and complete for all participants.

signalling.question: Clear definition of the prognostic factor, measured at a defined time?
signalling.quote: all measured at the time of the first MCI classification

signalling.question: Same valid method and adequate proportion with complete data?
signalling.quote: Age at first MCI diagnosis (y), m (std) ... missing 0 (0.0)

domains.rationale: Reversion is defined clearly and classified by a blinded algorithm on normed tests. However, visit frequency depends on age (every 3 years over 78, every 6 years under 78), so participants of different ages have different chances of being observed as reverted. Repeated testing also adds practice effects.

signalling.question: Clear definition of the outcome?
signalling.quote: Reverters were defined as participants that fulfilled all criteria for MCI, but no longer met the requirement for objective cognitive impairment

signalling.question: Valid and reliable method, blind to prior status?
signalling.quote: An algorithmic approach, blind to prior diagnosis, was applied retrospectively.

signalling.question: Same method and setting of outcome ascertainment for all participants?
signalling.quote: Follow-up visits were made every third year for those older than 78 years and every sixth year for those younger than 78.

signalling.question: Outcome free from measurement artefacts such as practice effects?
signalling.quote: exposing them to multiple testing sessions, potentially leading to practice effects that masked true decline [57].

domains.rationale: The age IRR is adjusted for a pre-specified set of sociodemographic, lifestyle, health and cognitive-severity variables.

signalling.question: Important potential confounders measured and accounted for?
signalling.quote: The baseline variables included in the model were sex, age, years of formal education, cohabitant, physical activity, alcohol consumption, BMI, cardiovascular disease, smoking status, sleep disturbances, number of cognitive domains affected, and depression.

signalling.question: Confounders defined and measured validly?
signalling.quote: Physical activity, cohabitation, smoking status, alcohol consumption, and years of formal education were self-reported.

domains.rationale: The model suits the design (Poisson with a follow-up offset and robust variance) and all covariates are reported. However, missing-data handling is not described. Competing outcomes are excluded rather than modelled. The reported figures are inconsistent in places: 42.4% in the text against 43.4% in the results, and transposed counts in the Table 2 standard row.

signalling.question: Selected statistical model adequate for the design?
signalling.quote: To acknowledge that the participants had different follow-up times, the time from the first MCI visit to the end of the follow-up, or incidence of reversion, whichever occurred first, was added as an offset. A robust variance estimator was implemented.

signalling.question: No selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: Two separate multivariate Poisson regression models including all covariates were run for the Petersen and the NP criteria, respectively (Table 4). ... Age (y) 1.02 (1.01; 1.03) <0.001***

signalling.question: Missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for imputation, complete-case analysis or a missing-data strategy; Table 1 lists missing counts but no handling method is described.

signalling.question: Data presented consistently enough to assess the analysis?
signalling.quote: Our reversion rates of 42.4% and 48.3% are higher than the 25% established in a meta-analysis

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS: attrition high; participation, outcome measurement and statistical analysis moderate)
overall_rationale: Study attrition is high because fewer than half of the MCI cases reach the analysis, and exclusion is related to age and to health status. The authors themselves read the age-reversion association as probably a follow-up artefact. Three further domains are moderate, which also meets this review's threshold for high.

applicability.rationale: The reversion rates are proportions among cases still eligible at follow-up, compared only with stable MCI; progressors and ADL decliners are excluded. 'Frequent reversion' therefore applies to that denominator.
